title: HIGH ACCURACY TESTING OF INTERFEROMETRIC ANTENNA WITH LARGE BASELINE - EXPRO PLUS
description: Future high frequency interferometric antennas (e.g. at Ka band) using large baselines require verification and testing with a veryhigh accuracy, in particular in phase. While such interferometric testing and ground calibration techniques have been successfully performed in the past (i.e. Cryosat), the consideration for baselines above 10 or 20 meters brings challenges in the ground validation in several domains: the antenna alignment, the boom effect on the antenna pattern and the synchronous co-alignment between all beams being generated are areas that require development toachieve satisfactory results, in line with the requirements. In addition, for baselines in the 15-20 meter range, the currently existing test facilities and techniques do not allow testing the complete baseline in deployed configuration. One of the solutions is to scale down the antenna sub-system, which would imply a measurement at frequencies in the order of a few hundred gigahertz - a challenge that once overcome, would allow a proper on ground characterisation ofthe complete system.A demonstrator of the scaled antenna sub-system shall be made available and tested to validate the testing conceptThe workflow of the activity is as follows:1) Identification of accuracy requirements and problem areas in large Ka band SAR interferometers2) Trade-off on verifications and testing methodologies3) Design and manufacture of scaled breadboard4) Testing ofbreadboard to validate concept

title: ALLOY DEVELOPMENT FOR HIGH PRESSURE AND OXYGEN RICH ENVIRONMENT PROPULSION EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop new European alloys for high-pressure, oxygen-rich propulsion applications, enhancing performance, manufacturability and supply chain resilience for next-generation launch vehicles.Description: Propulsion remains a key driver in launch vehicle performance, particularly as the sector pursues higher thrust capabilities through operation at elevated temperatures. Applications such as high-thrust engines, oxygen-rich pre-burners (used in staged combustion), gas generators, and high-pressure liquid oxygen (LOx) turbopumps must operate under extreme thermal and mechanical loads in highly reactive environments. At present, Europe lacks a material solution capable of meeting these demands. ESA teams, across several directorates have jointly identified this as a critical capability gap. While progress has been made in non-member states countries, Europe currently lacks materials capable of operating reliably in oxygen-rich and high-pressure environments. The development of tailored European alloy systems would directly support ongoing launcher developments, both from established industry and emerging companies working on micro, small and medium launch vehicles. These materials would serve as a strategic enabler across the sector, particularly for reusable platforms. The activity aimsto develop novel high-performance alloys suitable for use in oxygen-rich and high-pressure environments. These alloys must offer high thermal conductivity, mechanical strength at elevated temperatures, and compatibility with additive manufacturing (AM). Candidatematerial families include refractory alloys, superalloys, and oxide-dispersion-strengthened (ODS) alloys. Computational tools, including artificial intelligence (AI), will guide the design process to optimise performance and manufacturability while ensuring alignment with European supply chain capabilities. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define propulsion application requirements (temperature, duration, material compatibility, structural loads). - Conduct state-of-the-art assessment across candidate alloy families. - Use AI to support design of new alloy compositions meeting propulsion and AM requirements. - Produce experimental powder batches for selected alloy formulations. - Manufacture and test printed coupons in representative operational environments. -Evaluate manufacturability, including welding compatibility and potential for repair. - Perform preliminary life cycle analysis and assess European sourcing of raw elements. - Outline a roadmap for further maturation in subsequent projects.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. description: Nærværende projekt er en del af Forsvarskommandoens og ETK's samlede plan for "Faciliteter til Hærens Tunge Brigade" (FHTB) FHTB omfatter ombygning og nybygning på en række etablissementer rundt i landet, som skal sikre faciliteterne til Hærens Tunge Brigade. Nærværende udbud vedrører hovedentreprisen på 582 Aalborg Kaserne. Byggeriet på Aalborg Kaserne omfatter følgende: Projektet omfatter opførelse af to identiske garagebygninger med tilhørende kontortårne. Hver bygning består af en central garagefacilitet til understøttelse af den daglige drift samt to integrerede kontortårne i tre etager placeret i bygningens ender. Kontortårnene indeholder arbejdspladser, møde- og undervisningsfaciliteter samt de nødvendige velfærdsfunktioner, herunder opholdsrum, omklædning og øvrige personalefaciliteter. Garagebygningerne indrettes til køretøjer, materiel og tilhørende driftsfunktioner, mens kontortårnene samler de administrative funktioner og skaber moderne rammer for både ledelse, planlægning og personale. Bygningernes udformning sikrer en funktionel sammenhæng mellem drifts- og kontorfunktioner samt gode interne forbindelser mellem arbejdsområderne. Projektet omfatter også manøvre- og kørselsarealer omkring bygningerne, som sikrer adgang og effektiv drift for større køretøjer. Derudover etableres P Syd, en større parkeringsplads til lastbiler og andre tunge køretøjer. Området indrettes med fokus på trafiksikkerhed og funktionalitet, herunder tydelig adskillelse af kørende og gående trafik samt sikre gangforbindelser mellem parkeringsarealerne, bygningerne og områdets øvrige funktioner. title: FKZ 3726 26 301 0 - Analyse der Potenziale von Gruben-, Bergbau- und Sümpfungswasser in Deutschland
description: REFOPLAN 2026: „Analyse der Potenziale von Gruben-, Bergbau- und Sümpfungswasser in Deutschland“ In ganz Deutschland findet Ressourcengewinnung durch Bergbau statt - in unterschiedlichen Arten nach unterschiedlichen Ressourcen in unterschiedlicher Menge, je nach Vorkommen der Rohstoffe. Unter anderem greift der Rohstoffabbau in den Gewässerhaushalt ein. Angeschnittene Grundwasserleiter machen es erforderlich, in der aktiven Phase des Bergbaus und nach Einstellung des Betriebs mit dem Wasser umzugehen. Das Projekt prüft, welche Nutzungspotenziale Gruben-, Sümpfungs- und Bergbauwasser in sich trägt und wie diese Potenziale zum Schutz von Mensch und Umwelt genutzt werden können. Das zu erstellende Gutachten soll helfen, ungenutzte Potenziale zu identifizieren, Nutzungsvorschläge zu unterbreiten und Instrumente vorzuschlagen, wie diese Nutzung auch wirtschaftlich gelingt. Dazu trägt das Gutachten Daten und Fakten zusammen, unter anderem zur Zusammensetzung des Bergbauwassers (als Ergebnis einer Datenrecherche, keine eigene Analytik) und erhebt die Potenziale des Bergbauwassers für die Rohstoffgewinnung und zur energetischen Nutzung. Es beschreibt praktizierte Wassermanagementmaßnahmen an ausgewählten Standorten in Deutschland sowie Potenziale der Bergbaustandorte als Retentionsräume, insb. bei Starkregenereignissen. Neben der Begutachtung der genannten Frage- und Problemstellungen visualisiert das Projekt Bergbaustandorte mit den jeweiligen Wasserqualitäten und -managementmaßnahmen in GIS-fähigen Karten und betreibt diese Karten für die Projektlaufzeit.
